title: footgun: `assertValidProjectModules` — the name promises it asserts every listed module is valid and rejects otherwise.
detail: A non-semantic module that fails `ModuleCartridgeSchema` makes `parseProjectModuleFile` return null (projectModuleParsing.ts:25), which the try/catch does not catch; line 95 `if (module)` then silently skips it, so an invalid module is dropped from the returned map without any error. It only throws for a missing file (line 88) or a thrown ZodError.

title: footgun: `for (const [path, mod] of pending.entries())` then `writeModule(path, ...)` — the variable named `path` reads like a resolved absolute file path.
detail: `pending` is keyed by `nextFile`, a project-relative filename (set at line 51), and `writeModule`'s parameter is `filename`. The value is a relative name, not a path; `writeModule` itself resolves it via resolveProjectFile. The name contradicts what it holds.

title: footgun: `stageProjectVersion(manifestPath, currentManifestVersion, changeKind)` reads like a pure function of its arguments.
detail: It reads and mutates the module-level `stagedVersions` Map (process-global singleton). The `currentManifestVersion` argument is ignored on every call after the first for a given path — subsequent bumps are computed from the cached `baseVersion`, not the passed-in version, so passing an updated current version has no effect once a bump is staged.

title: Namespace rename matches by prefix, corrupting sibling namespaces
detail: `ns.startsWith(oldNamespace)` and `replaceRefs`/filename `.replace(oldNamespace, ...)` treat the namespace as a bare prefix/substring: renaming `foo` also rewrites `foobar`, `foo2`, and any `foo::`-prefixed ref inside an unrelated `foobarbaz::` string. Unrelated modules get silently moved and their refs mangled.

title: String.replace rewrites only the first occurrence of a namespace
detail: `filename.replace(oldNamespace, newNamespace)` (line 41) and `file.replace(oldNamespace, newNamespace)` (line 65) use the single-match form of replace. If a filename or manifest entry contains the old namespace more than once, only the first is rewritten, leaving a half-renamed path that no longer resolves. `replaceRefs` uses replaceAll and is correct, so refs and filenames diverge.

title: Global staged-version Map leaks and cross-contaminates instances
detail: `stagedVersions` is a module-level Map shared by every WorkspaceService/RefactorService in the process. Entries are only removed by explicit clearStagedProjectVersion, so an abandoned project (or a test that stages but never persists) leaks its entry forever, and two consumers acting on the same manifestPath see each other's pending bump. In tests this makes version-staging order-dependent and stateful across cases.

title: Manifest re-read via readFile can silently reset the manifest to empty
detail: `(await this.vfs.readFile(manifestPath)) ?? { files: [] }` uses FileSystemBase.readFile, which returns null when the stored value is a string / only present on the text path (FileSystem.base.ts:57,66). On that path the fallback `{ files: [] }` is written back, discarding the real name, version, and file list — a full manifest wipe. loadProject uses readProjectManifest (object-or-text aware) but this refactor path does not.

title: Runtime rebuilt from an arbitrary first cache entry
detail: `replaceRuntime` seeds a new Runtime from `Array.from(this.moduleCache.values())[0]` — the first module by Map insertion order, not the linked/compiled cartridge (activeCartridge) and not a designated entry module. Which single module becomes the runtime depends on manifest.files ordering, and the compiled activeCartridge produced by the linker is not what the runtime runs.

title: silent failure: ignored-return
detail: Real. `parseProjectModuleFile` returns null when a non-semantic module fails ModuleCartridgeSchema (projectModuleParsing.ts:25); the guard `if (module)` drops it with no throw and no log, so loadProject proceeds with an incomplete moduleCache and activeCartridge as if the invalid module never existed. A malformed module silently disappears from the project instead of failing the load.

title: silent failure: ignored-return
detail: Mostly benign but silent. `reloadModules` returns early when no project/root is loaded, doing nothing and returning void — a caller expecting the modules to have been reloaded gets no error and no signal that the reload was skipped.

title: silent failure: ignored-return
detail: Real. In reloadModules, `const mod = await this.vfs.readFile(...)` then `if (mod) this.moduleCache.set(...)`: a filename that reads back as null (missing on disk, or stored as a string so readFile returns null) is skipped silently, leaving the stale prior cache entry in place with no error, so the reload appears to succeed while that module is unchanged.
